sections.label: Administration of Muslim Law Act history
sections.summary: AMLA was enacted in Singapore's founding years so Muslims could have marriage, divorce and estates governed by Muslim law, and it established MUIS and the Mufti.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The Administration of Muslim Law Act was put in place during the founding years of our nation so that Muslims could continue to have matters pertaining to marriage, divorce and their estates governed by Muslim law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In the founding years of our nation, Mr Ahmad Ibrahim, the first Attorney-General of Singapore, and leaders from the Muslim Advisory Board, the All-Malaya Muslim Missionary Society, the Mohammadiah Movement and the Singapore Religious Teachers' Association, also known as PERGAS, led the effort in establishing a central and uniting voice to represent Muslims in religious affairs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Thus, AMLA established the Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura, also known as MUIS, to be the central administrative body for the Muslim community and designated the Mufti as the highest religious authority for Islam in Singapore.

sections.label: Minimum marriage age amendment
sections.summary: In 2008, this House amended AMLA to raise the minimum age of marriage under AMLA to 18 years to match the Women's Charter.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For example, in 2008, this House amended AMLA to raise the minimum age of marriage under AMLA to 18 years of age to match the Women's Charter.

sections.label: Amendments for SYC and ROMM
sections.summary: About half of the amendments seek to improve service delivery of SYC and ROMM and provide greater support to Muslim couples and families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: About half of the amendments seek to improve service delivery of SYC and ROMM and provide greater support to Muslim couples and families.

sections.label: Remote communication technology powers
sections.summary: The Bill gives SYC, an Appeal Board and ROMM permanent powers to conduct proceedings via remote communication technology in appropriate situations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We have learnt the importance of leveraging technology for contingencies so that we can minimise disruptions to service delivery.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Thus, this Bill contains amendments that will give SYC, an Appeal Board and ROMM permanent powers to conduct proceedings via remote communication technology in appropriate situations.

sections.label: Hakam divorce and registration fees
sections.summary: The law is proposed to be amended so SYC can work directly with the first set of hakam to authorise divorce, and clauses 8, 9 and 10 remove payment of fees as a condition for divorce registration.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: This can prolong the grief of parties, as this requires parties to go through the entire process again with the SYC-appointed hakam.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We are thus proposing to amend the law so that the SYC can work directly with the first set of hakam to authorise the hakam to pronounce the divorce, even if the husband refuses to authorise the hakam if it is in the interest of both parties to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Clauses 8, 9 and 10 work together to remove the payment of fees as a condition for the registration of a divorce to prevent abuse by parties who disagree with the SYC's decision.

sections.label: Therapeutic justice for divorcing families
sections.summary: Clauses 4, 5 and 6 allow Muslim families undergoing divorce to benefit from evidence-based therapeutic justice measures agreed with the Women's Charter (Amendment) Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: The last group of amendments I would like to draw the House's attention to are clauses 4, 5 and 6.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: These amendments allow Muslim families undergoing divorce to benefit from the evidence-based measures for therapeutic justice that this House agreed to last month with the Women's Charter (Amendment) Act.

sections.label: Remote marriages and divorces
sections.summary: The Bill introduces provisions allowing marriages and divorces via live video or television link, extending COVID-19 temporary measures and permitting remote divorces with Syariah Court permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: First, the Bill proposes to introduce new provisions to allow marriages and divorces to take place through a live video or television link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This not only makes permanent the temporary measures contained in the COVID-19 (Temporary Measures for Solemnisation and Registration of Marriages) Act 2020, in fact, it goes further to allow divorces to take place remotely with the permission of the Syariah Court.

sections.label: Hakam divorce amendment
sections.summary: The amendment to section 50 removes the need for a second set of hakam, empowering the first set to pronounce divorce if jointly of that opinion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One, the proposed amendment to section 50 removes the present need for the Syariah Court to appoint a second set of hakam, or arbitrators, to attempt reconciliation and pronounce divorce where reconciliation is not possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the amended procedure, the first set of hakam would be empowered to pronounce a divorce if they are of the joint opinion that the parties should be divorced.

sections.label: Enforcing divorce fees
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Syariah Court would enforce payment of fees, especially if the divorce has already been registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While I note the rationale that a party cannot be allowed to frustrate the divorce process by simply refusing to pay the fees, I would like to ask how the Syariah Court would go about enforcing the payment of such fees, especially if the divorce has already been registered.

sections.label: Children's support programme compliance
sections.summary: The speaker notes the Bill is silent on consequences if parties fail to comply with the Court's advice to secure children's completion of the support programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, the ability to ensure that these children receive the necessary support is important.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But what the Bill is silent on is: what consequences are there if parties fail to comply with the Court's advice to secure their children's completion of the support programme?

sections.label: Removing prescribed divorce form
sections.summary: Clause 22 of the Bill removes the requirement to use a prescribed form to apply for divorce or revocation of divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One, I notice that clause 22 of the Bill purports to remove the requirement to use a prescribed form to apply for divorce or revocation of divorce.

sections.label: Mufti evidence presumption
sections.summary: Clause 24 amends section 139(2) AMLA so the Mufti's evidence that a doctrine, ceremony or act is contrary to Muslim law is presumptively accepted by a criminal Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Two, clause 24 of the Bill proposes amending section 139(2) AMLA such that the Mufti's evidence that a doctrine, ceremony or act is contrary to the Muslim law shall be presumptively accepted by a criminal Court prosecuting an offence under section 139(1).

sections.label: Digital Syariah Court divorce access
sections.summary: The speaker is concerned that convenient digital access to the Syariah Court process can influence parties' assessment of wanting to divorce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My concern is that the convenient access to the Syariah Court process through digitalisation can influence the assessment of parties wishing to divorce.

sections.label: Convenience erases assessment space
sections.summary: Simplifying the Syariah Court process by digitalisation, easy with a click, erases space and time for divorcing parties to assess more deeply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By simplifying the Syariah Court process through digitalisation, which is made easy with a click of a button, this "convenience" factor will erase any additional space and time that could have enabled the divorcing parties to make a much deeper assessment.

sections.label: Ministry assurance on digital process
sections.summary: The Ministry assured that the Syariah Court and MUIS Appeal Board would use digital channels only if all parties agree.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Arising from this concern, the Ministry gave its assurance that the Syariah Court and the MUIS Appeal Board would conduct the process through digital channels only if all parties are agreeable.

sections.label: Clauses and registration fee appeals
sections.summary: This is stated in clauses 8, 9 and 10 of the amendment Bill, and some residents asked the speaker to appeal to set aside the registration fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is stated in clause 8, 9 and 10 of this amendment Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I was also approached by some residents who had difficulty paying the registration fee and asked me to appeal to the Syariah Court to set aside the registration fee.

sections.label: Section 45A electronic hearings
sections.summary: The insertion of section 45A provides that the SYC or Appeal Board may conduct hearings through electronic means of communication.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The insertion of section 45A provides that the SYC or Appeal Board may conduct hearings through electronic means of communication.

sections.label: US online hearing halted
sections.summary: An online court hearing in the US in March 2021 was halted when a prosecutor realised the victim and her abuser were in the same room.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: An online court hearing held in the US in March 2021 was halted when a prosecutor realised that the victim and her abuser were in the same room in her house.

sections.label: Deferring proceedings and live audio link
sections.summary: Asks whether parties may defer proceedings and whether SYC may proceed by live audio link with unanimous consent, and for public understanding of factors for deciding without oral arguments under section 35B.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, in the event there is no alternative device, would parties be permitted to defer the proceedings?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I also understand that, in such an event with all parties' unanimous consent, SYC may proceed with the remainder of the hearing through live audio link only, without an accompanying live video stream.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As we move forward with these changes, it will be useful for the public to also understand factors that are considered by SYC when deciding under what circumstances a matter will be decided without hearing oral arguments, as permitted with the insertion of section 35B.

sections.label: Support for children
sections.summary: Notes that support for children is becoming more explicit and expanded, as not all parents may be equipped to play professional caregiving roles.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am heartened that support for children is becoming more explicit and expanded.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is important, as, even though it was mentioned then that the bulk of responsibility should fall on the parents, during these difficult times, especially, not all parents may be sufficiently equipped to also play the roles of counsellor, psychiatrist and other roles for a child's care that may require a professional to better protect their well-being.

sections.label: Grief and stressors affecting compliance
sections.summary: States that grief and other stressors might make it difficult for parents to comply with the order even though they want the best for their children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Furthermore, even though parents want the best for their children, grief and other stressors might make it difficult for them to comply with the order.

sections.label: Tailored programmes and coordinated support
sections.summary: Asks how programmes will be tailor-made for the community and how support can be better coordinated in the child's best interest, while justice quality remains the priority.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the context of the amendments at hand, how will the programmes be tailor-made for our community and how can support be better coordinated in the best interest of the child?

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While so much has been made possible and more convenient with digitalisation and broader access to support programmes, it is important that the interests and quality of justice remain the overriding priority in this case.

sections.label: Digital processes for Court and ROMM
sections.summary: The amendment allows the Syariah Court and the Registry of Muslim Marriages to use digital processes for Court administration and solemnisations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In particular, the amendment allows the Syariah Court and the Registry of Muslim Marriages (ROMM) to use digital processes for Court administration and solemnisations.

sections.label: Section 35B without oral arguments
sections.summary: The amendment to section 35B allows the Syariah Court or the Appeal Board to proceed without hearing oral arguments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, the amendment to section 35B allows the Syariah Court or the Appeal Board to proceed without hearing oral arguments.

sections.label: Publishing Syariah Court decision grounds
sections.summary: A suggestion is made that the Syariah Court and Appeal Board openly publish reasons and grounds of decisions for every case on the MUIS or Syariah Court website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: We should not pursue efficiency and effectiveness in the administration of Court processes, at the expense of losing what we already have.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I suggest that the Syariah Court and the Appeal Board openly publish the reasons and grounds of decisions for every case on the MUIS or Syariah Court's website.

sections.label: Hakam divorce without full authority
sections.summary: The proposed amendment states a hakam may pronounce a divorce in the absence of full authority from their principals, even if the husband refuses to sign or delegate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The MUIS Appeal Board case of Azman bin Abdul Rani v Rahmah bte Ramli (1998) 1 SSAR 93 seems to suggest that this delegation is critical.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the proposed amendment which states that the hakam may pronounce a divorce in the absence of full authority from their respective principals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, even if the husband refuses to sign the form or delegate his power, the hakam may pronounce a divorce in certain cases.

sections.label: Restricting access to marriage register
sections.summary: The current amendment aims to restrict access to the Register of Muslim Marriages only.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The current amendment aims to restrict access to the Register of Muslim Marriages only.

sections.label: Classes of persons allowed access
sections.summary: A question is asked about what the classes of persons allowed access to the Register of Marriages are.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to ask: what are the "classes of persons" allowed access to the Register of Marriages?

sections.label: Mufti replacing MUIS President
sections.summary: The current amendment replaces the MUIS President with the Mufti so the Mufti can provide evidence directly to Court on matters contrary to Muslim law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The current amendment, which replaces the MUIS President with the Mufti, so that the Mufti can provide evidence directly to Court on matters that are contrary to Muslim law, is a welcomed one.

sections.label: New Syariah Court IT system
sections.summary: SYC will replace its old case management system with a new IT system to improve case management and communication with Court users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: First, SYC will replace its old case management system with a new IT system to improve case management and communication with Court users.

sections.label: Electronic court and marriage solemnisations
sections.summary: The Bill allows SYC and ROMM to conduct Court proceedings and marriage solemnisations electronically, after about 100 couples married digitally since May 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Second, this Bill will allow SYC and ROMM to conduct Court proceedings and marriage solemnisations via electronic means of communication in appropriate situations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Since May 2020, close to 100 couples or about 1% of total Muslim marriages, have conducted their marriage solemnisation through digital means during the COVID-19 pandemic.

sections.label: Virtual hearings not default
sections.summary: Virtual proceedings using electronic communication are neither the norm nor the default mode for hearings in the Court and before an Appeal Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat's question, proceedings that are held virtually using electronic means of communication are neither the norm nor the default mode for hearings in the Court and before an Appeal Board.

sections.label: Deciding matters without oral hearing
sections.summary: New section 35B enables the Court or Appeal Board to decide any matter without an oral hearing and asynchronously in a suitable case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The new section 35B is an enabling provision to allow the Court or Appeal Board to decide any matter without an oral hearing and asynchronously, in a suitable case.

sections.label: Plaintiff consent for asynchronous proceedings
sections.summary: The Court must obtain the Plaintiff's consent to waive the right to continue the oral hearing before proceeding asynchronously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The Court is required to obtain the consent of the Plaintiff to waive his or her right to continue with the oral hearing before the Court may proceed to conduct the remaining part of the proceedings in an asynchronous manner.

sections.label: Physical hearing if fairness impacted
sections.summary: Where a virtual hearing may impact fairness, SYC will arrange a physical hearing, with the SYC Court house as default location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: For any reason where a virtual hearing may impact the fairness of the proceedings, SYC will arrange for a physical hearing, where the Court house of SYC is the default location.

sections.label: Electronic filing in subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: The detailed implementation of the new electronic filing system will be set out in subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The detailed implementation of the new electronic filing system will be set out in the subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Who may act in marriage
sections.summary: Only parties to the marriage and their family members may do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Only parties to the marriage and family members of parties to the marriage may do so.

sections.label: Hakam deadlock divorce cases
sections.summary: Cases where both hakam agree on divorce for irreconcilable differences but the husband refuses talak number under 1% a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The number of cases in which hakam for the husband and hakam for the wife are jointly of the opinion that parties should be divorced because they are in a state of irreconcilable differences but the husband refuses to pronounce talak or authorise his hakam to do so, is less than 1% a year.

sections.label: Divorce registration fee technicality
sections.summary: Under current provisions divorce is registered upon payment of an administrative fee, a technicality the amendment rectifies by delinking payment from the Court's power to order registration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: To Mr Saktiandi Supaat's query, under current provisions, a divorce is registered upon payment of an administrative fee.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This is a technicality that the amendment seeks to rectify by delinking payment of the divorce registration fee with the Court's power to order the registration of the divorce.

sections.label: Amicable divorce settlements
sections.summary: More than half of divorces registered in the past five years are settled amicably on all issues relating to the divorce application.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More than half of the divorces registered in the past five years are settled amicably on all issues relating to the divorce application.

sections.label: Scope of section 32(7)
sections.summary: Section 32(7) is very wide, covering Muslim law, and invokes no presumption favouring the Legal Committee's opinion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: Section 32(7) is very wide, as it covers the question of Muslim law and it does not invoke any presumption in favour of the opinion provided by the Legal Committee, also known as the Fatwa Committee.

sections.label: Mufti evidence and Muslim law opinions
sections.summary: The amendment lets the Mufti give evidence in lieu of the President of MUIS, and section 32(7) applies if the Court requests the Majlis's opinion on Muslim law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: The amendment seeks to allow the Mufti, which is the highest Muslim religious authority in Singapore, to give evidence in lieu of the President of MUIS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: More broadly, if the Court requests for the opinion of the Majlis on any question on Muslim law, section 32(7) would apply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: I also thank Mr Zhulkarnain Aabdul Rahim for his suggestion on section 114 of AMLA to make Mufti the reference for Muslim law questions on inheritance and succession.

sentences.speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
sentences.text: This Bill will help our Muslim institutions to better serve the community, improve legal processes, and strengthen the social support given to families and children.
